current_plan.body:
ANALYZE the specified
O(n) worst‑case time, stability, in‑place operation, O(1) extra space, and comparison‑based nature.
EVALUATE theoretical lower bounds for comparison‑based sorting to determine feasibility of O(n) worst‑case time.
IF the constraints are jointly feasible THEN
DESIGN a high‑level algorithmic strategy that achieves the required time, stability, and space properties without implementing concrete code.
OUTLINE the steps of the algorithm in abstract form, referencing required operations (e.g., partitioning, merging) while preserving stability and in‑place execution.
ELSE
PREPARE a concise explanation of why the constraints cannot be satisfied simultaneously, citing the relevant lower‑bound arguments.
END IF

parsed.body: The specified constraints cannot all be satisfied simultaneously. For comparison‑based sorting algorithms, the decision‑tree lower bound guarantees a worst‑case time complexity of Ω(n log n). Therefore achieving O(n) worst‑case time while remaining comparison‑based is impossible, regardless of stability, in‑place operation, or extra‑space usage. Consequently no algorithm can meet all four requirements together.
